title: MoralDial: A Framework to Train and Evaluate Moral Dialogue Systems via Moral Discussions
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures a dialogue system's alignment with general moral and social norms (termed Rules of Thumb or RoTs). It specifically evaluates the ability to provide safe answers (Safety Score), offer logically self-consistent moral explanations (ME Score), revise moral standpoints when presented with conflicting user values (MR Score), and consistently apply a moral rule to new scenarios (RIL Score). It does not specifically measure any aspect of faith or religion.
findings: The paper does not investigate religion and therefore presents no findings related to it. The paper's findings indicate that its proposed framework, MORALDIAL, significantly improves the moral alignment of dialogue models like DialoGPT and BlenderBot. The trained models showed substantial gains in safety (SMA score), moral explanation (SME score), and moral inference (SRIL score) compared to their baseline versions, without degrading general conversational ability.
